name: Five-scene business explainer
summary: A bold five-scene explainer: problem, solution, three steps, one proof, name.
bestFor: Small businesses explaining what they do in half a minute
prompt: Build a 30-second explainer for a fictional bookkeeping studio in five scenes. Scene one states the customer's problem in big bold text. Scene two says what the studio does. Scene three shows how it works in three numbered steps. Scene four gives one proof point as a quote. The last scene ends on the studio name. Smooth transitions, brand colours.

name: One-shape UI morph promo
summary: A single shape morphs through every product state while a cursor clicks and drags it.
bestFor: SaaS teams showing a full workflow in one unbroken shot
prompt: Make a loopable square product promo for a fictional ad-launch tool using one shape that never cuts. The same rounded element morphs in size, radius and colour as its content swaps with a short blur. A large cursor drives each change: connect accounts, type a prompt, approve, drag a budget slider, flip a toggle. Camera zooms so each state fills the frame, and the last frame matches the first.

name: Story-led launch film
summary: A 30-second launch film that moves from why it matters to pain, fix and payoff, ending on a logo reveal.
bestFor: SaaS founders launching a product from a landing page
prompt: Create a 30-second launch film for a fictional project-tracking app in four or five scenes, each with one short title. Tell it as one story: why teams care, why it hurts today, how the app fixes it, what you get. Kinetic typography word by word, springy easing, gentle camera pushes, and elements that build in on the beat. Hold each scene long enough to read, then end on an animated logo, tagline and web address.

name: Campaign workflow demo
summary: A punchy walkthrough of one user going from campaign setup through to results, screen by screen.
bestFor: Marketing and analytics tools showing an end-to-end workflow
prompt: Make a slick, punchy 45-second walkthrough for a fictional marketing analytics tool. One user creates an ad campaign, connects their metrics, sees where results come from, then connects a voice assistant that replies to a lead and follows up. A person approves the reply before it goes out. Finish on the analytics dashboard. Show each step on a clean UI screen with a cursor.

name: Premium brand showreel
summary: A restrained, expensive-feeling 15-second film that presents a product with calm editorial polish.
bestFor: Finance or utility apps wanting a mature, high-end image
prompt: Create a 15-second premium brand film for a fictional invoicing app. Treat it as a quiet editorial showreel, not a feature walkthrough. Use large still compositions, fine type, generous negative space, and a few real-feeling UI cards that slide in and settle. Cuts land on a soft beat. The viewer should think this is a surprisingly elegant tool. End on the wordmark.

name: Bold manifesto typography
summary: A 20-second type-only manifesto where one statement builds word by word with hard, confident beats.
bestFor: Mission-driven startups and campaigns stating a belief
prompt: Make a 20-second manifesto video for a fictional open-science collective. One belief, "knowledge should belong to everyone", is built in big typography across short scenes. Words slam in on the beat, key words change colour, and a final line holds still before the name appears. No images, only text and simple shapes, with sound hits matching each word.

name: Festival story explainer
summary: A warm short story explaining a festival, from old tradition to family reunion.
bestFor: Cultural, seasonal and educational content
prompt: Make a 30-second animated story explaining a harvest moon festival. Start with how the tradition began long ago, move through the foods and lanterns, and arrive at families gathering. Soft hand-drawn moon, lanterns and tables, gentle narration, and a closing line that no distance should keep us from the people we miss.

name: Zoom-through product reveal
summary: A camera-led reveal that grows from one dot into a workspace, then dives into a phone.
bestFor: Trading, analytics and dashboard products with several panels
prompt: Make a 30-second product reveal for a fictional trading workspace. Start with a single dot on a black screen. Panels open one by one: charts, positions, a watchlist. The camera zooms in and out at different scales, then pulls back until the desktop is a point in space, and dives into a phone screen showing the same chart. End on the line that everything fits on one screen.

name: Punchy startup launch
summary: A fast, slick launch film with big claims and hard cuts, ending on the product name.
bestFor: AI and infrastructure startups announcing a product
prompt: Make a slick, punchy 20 second launch video for a fictional startup that makes AI answers arrive faster. Open with one blunt claim, then cut through three short feature beats on big type, each landing on a hit. Dark and light switches keep it moving. Finish on the name and one short call to action.

name: Motion designer showreel
summary: A fast personal showreel of kinetic type, shapes and transitions that proves a designer's range.
bestFor: Motion designers and studios building a reel
prompt: Make a 15 second showreel for a fictional motion designer. Pack in quick demonstrations of range: kinetic type, shape morphs, a stat count, a logo reveal and a liquid transition. Every second introduces a new idea with a hard switch between light and dark. End on the designer's name and a hiring line.

name: Overthinking concept reel
summary: A showreel built around one idea, loops of looping thoughts told through restless type and shapes.
bestFor: Designers turning an abstract feeling into motion
prompt: Make a 15 second concept reel about overthinking. Show one simple thought that spirals, repeats and tangles through scribbled loops and growing type, then snaps into a single calm line. Fast cuts at first, then a held stillness. Use hand-drawn marks and a restrained palette.

name: SaaS launch video
summary: A professional launch film that shows features and benefits as fast motion-graphics scenes.
bestFor: SaaS founders launching a product on social
prompt: Make a 30 second launch video for a fictional scheduling app. Open on the pain of double bookings, then reveal the product with a click on a calendar, show three features as quick UI scenes, and state the benefit in one line of big type. Close on the logo and a sign-up line.

name: Open-source README hero
summary: A short hero loop for a code project, three steps in a punchy line, then the install call.
bestFor: Open-source maintainers needing a README hero video
prompt: Make a 20 second hero video for a fictional open-source command line tool. Show the idea in three beats: give it a site, write a goal, watch it act. Use a terminal window with typed text and a cursor that clicks through the steps. End on the project name and the install line.

name: Paper marker launch
summary: A paper-light film with marker notes that draw on, huge type and hard light-dark switches.
bestFor: Founders who want a hand-made explainer feel
prompt: Make a 15 second explainer for a fictional note-taking tool. Use a paper canvas with marker notes that draw on, huge condensed type, and a new idea every second and a half. Switch hard to charcoal for the key claim. Name what the product learns, claim no figures, and end on the wordmark.

name: Why we're best loop
summary: A square looping showreel with a one-second hook that argues why a product wins at one thing.
bestFor: Brands needing a looping proof post for feeds
prompt: Make a 15 second square looping video that argues why a fictional coffee grinder is best at even grinding. Hook in the first second with one bold claim, then three fast proof beats built from simple shapes and type, and end on a frame that matches the first so it loops.

name: Typographic speech film
summary: A short speech built from type where each key word becomes part of the structure it stands on.
bestFor: Campaign films and manifesto openers
prompt: Make a 20 second square film of a short original speech told only in type. Each line rearranges the frame: one word becomes a beam, another a hanging weight, another a support, and the last word becomes a floor the final line stands on. Dark green ground, cream paper, one amber accent.

name: Pencil data story
summary: A hand-drawn pencil animation that charts a topic across years, with a tasteful colour fringe.
bestFor: Explaining a trend over time with a data story
prompt: Make a 90 second pencil-drawn data story about a fictional city's summer temperatures. Start with a hand-drawn thermometer, then draw a line chart year by year, mark the hottest summer with a circle, and compare it with earlier years on a second line. Use a faint colour fringe and end on one plain takeaway.

name: Recursion explainer
summary: A fast, clever explainer where each explanation of recursion arrives in a completely different visual style.
bestFor: Educators and explainer channels with a twist
prompt: Make a 45 second explainer about recursion where every explanation uses a different visual style: a sketch of nested boxes, a terminal with a function calling itself, a dictionary entry that points to itself, then a final card that explains recursion by repeating the video. Keep it quick and self-referential.

name: Ecosystem explainer
summary: A calm illustrated explainer that shows how one living system supports many others, with a soft score.
bestFor: Science teachers and nature channels
prompt: Make a 45 second explainer on how a tree works as an ecosystem. Draw the tree, then reveal roots sharing nutrients, birds nesting in branches, insects in bark and fallen leaves feeding the soil. Use gentle hand-drawn lines, one label per idea and a soft musical bed. End on one thought about connection.

name: Everyday spending reel
summary: A vertical reel that simulates a day of purchases at a shop, a fuel stop and a restaurant.
bestFor: Finance and card apps making vertical social ads
prompt: Make a 20 second vertical reel for a fictional spending app. Show three everyday stops, a grocery run, a fuel stop and a dinner, each as a phone screen where a payment is made and a running total counts up. Keep it modern and elegant, and end on the app name and a download line.

name: Developer tool launch
summary: A fast, precise launch film for a developer library, built for a keynote opening or social feed.
bestFor: Developer-tools companies launching a library
prompt: Make a 15 second launch film for a fictional developer library that helps build chat features. Use fast type, a code editor that types a few lines, and a toggle that swaps between providers with one click. Keep it precise and polished, with a restrained electronic pulse that builds to the name.

name: App launch showreel
summary: A vertical French-language app launch reel over a dark sunburst, with a leaderboard card and a download call.
bestFor: Consumer apps launching with a short vertical promo
prompt: Make a 15 second vertical showreel for the launch of a fictional daily brain-game app, with all text in French. Open on a bold line about a daily competition over a dark burgundy sunburst, slide in a tilted leaderboard card with players and scores, then show two more feature moments such as streaks and friend challenges. Cream serif headlines with one italic accent, cuts on the beat, and end on the app name with a download call.

name: Feature tour promo
summary: A professional promo that walks through a project's main features on screen, one per beat.
bestFor: Software projects needing a feature overview film
prompt: Make a 30 second widescreen promo that introduces a fictional project management tool by its key features. Give each feature its own beat with big type and a quick UI demonstration, a board, a timeline and a share action. Close with the name, a one-line promise and a call to action.

name: Paper-style product launch
summary: A ten-scene launch video in a paper style that covers problem, product and payoff.
bestFor: Solo founders launching without a designer
prompt: Make a 30 second launch video for a fictional website redesign tool in a paper-cut style. Scenes: the ugly old page, the problem in one line, a click that starts the redesign, a before and after swap, three small benefits, and the name. Keep each scene about three seconds with a cut-paper wipe between.

name: Article to lesson
summary: An educational video that turns one article into a clear sequence of key points, each with a simple visual.
bestFor: Teachers and publishers repurposing written content
prompt: Make a 60 second educational video from a short article about how vaccines train the immune system. Pull out four key ideas in order, give each a title, one plain sentence and a simple animated diagram, and finish with a summary card that repeats the ideas in one line each.

name: Slow-camera product teaser
summary: A calm, polished teaser: lowercase lines, a fast spinning list, then one slow camera reveal.
bestFor: Software launches that solve a modern pain point
prompt: A 27 second silent teaser for a desktop organiser app, all copy lowercase. Open on a big line entering word by word with a colour wipe. Scale it above a fast spinning list of everyday work annoyances that lands slowly on one phrase, then a question mark pops. Pull back to show app windows piling in, push through, and resolve on the product name. Slow ease-in-out moves, light grain.

name: SaaS use-case montage
summary: A modern SaaS montage that rattles through many real-world uses of one tool in quick, clean beats.
bestFor: Utility and developer tools with several distinct use cases
prompt: A 20 second modern SaaS video for an email checking tool, in the confident style of startup launch clips. Hook with the problem of bounced emails, then fire through quick scenes for sign-up forms, sales outreach, newsletters and event lists, each showing a list being cleaned on screen. End on the product name and a simple call to action.

name: Three-step doodle how-to
summary: A hand-drawn three-step walkthrough where each step is sketched in and numbered, ending with a go-live.
bestFor: Onboarding flows that take three simple steps
prompt: A 30 second hand-drawn animated clip showing how to list a product on a deals marketplace using an AI agent. Step one, connect your agent. Step two, the agent fills out the listing and sets up redemption. Step three, go live. Each step is sketched in with a big number and a tiny doodled scene, ending on a cheerful launch.

name: Life-cycle loop story
summary: A wordless-feeling life story that follows one figure from childhood to old age, then loops back to the start.
bestFor: Brand stories about time, legacy or long-term care
prompt: A 20 second looping motion story following one simple figure through the stages of life: childhood play, teenage years, the nine-to-five grind, family life, old age, then a quiet fade. Each stage is a short vivid scene with one label, and the final cut returns to the first frame so the video loops seamlessly.

name: Key moments timeline
summary: A horizontal timeline that steps through landmark moments of one field, each with a year and a short label.
bestFor: History explainers and company or industry milestone reels
prompt: A 40 second timeline video about key moments in the history of computing. A line draws across the screen and stops at five milestones, each with a large year, a short label and a simple icon built from shapes. The pace quickens toward the present and closes on a question about what comes next.

name: Derivative concept explainer
summary: A friendly maths explainer building the derivative from a worked example and a closing question.
bestFor: Teachers and course creators explaining a core concept
prompt: A 90 second voiceover explainer introducing the derivative in plain language. Start with a car whose speed changes, draw its distance curve, then zoom into a tiny stretch until the curve looks like a straight line and show that slope as the speed. Work one simple example on screen and finish with a question that makes viewers think.

name: Love-note mascot story
summary: A short vertical story about a mascot sending love notes through a mailbox, ending on a soft app tease.
bestFor: Consumer apps with a character and a warm, playful tone
prompt: A 9:16 short story with sound effects about a little pig who slips love notes into a mailbox for his partner. Show him writing, posting, waiting, then the partner finding each note with a happy reaction. Keep it fun and quick, and end with a gentle tease for the couples app that inspired it.

name: Ask-and-appear demo
summary: A product clip where a person asks for branded images and watches them drop straight into their content.
bestFor: AI content tools that generate and place assets
prompt: A 20 second animated clip for a content tool with built-in image generation. A user types a request for branded images, the images appear one by one, and each slides into a social post and a blog layout. Show the request, the result and the finished content with a click-driven cursor.

name: Podcast-snippet product ad
summary: An ad built as a story from short spoken-word snippets, each line setting up what the product solves.
bestFor: Audio and note-taking products with a relatable pain
prompt: A 30 second ad for an audio app made as a story from short quoted lines of talk shows. Each line appears as an animated caption over a waveform and builds up the same problem: great ideas heard and then forgotten. Resolve with the product saving a moment with one tap and end on its name.

name: Hook-proof-AI launch
summary: A quick-cut social launch video: a first-second hook, product proof scenes, then an AI feature beat.
bestFor: Product launches aimed at social feeds
prompt: A 25 second social launch video for an interactive demo-making tool. Hook in the first second with a bold claim, then give distinct beats for product proof showing a click-through demo being built, and a beat for the AI feature that writes the steps. Quick cuts, confident type, and a final call to action.

name: Multi-length launch ad
summary: A beat-locked launch ad built to be cut into short, vertical-safe versions with big captions.
bestFor: News, media and subscription products on social
prompt: A 30 second launch ad for a news digest app on a steady 120 BPM grid, with every cut on the beat. Big captions fit inside the vertical safe zone. Scenes move from the problem of too many headlines to the app sorting them into one calm briefing, then the name and a call to action. The same scenes can be trimmed into 15 and 6 second cuts.

name: Earthquake physics explainer
summary: A clear diagram-led explainer showing how strain builds along a fault and releases as an earthquake.
bestFor: Science educators and learning platforms
prompt: A 45 second animated explainer on how earthquakes happen. Draw two blocks of crust pressing past each other along a fault, show a strain curve slowly building, then snapping when the fault slips and waves spread outward. Label each stage plainly and finish with a calm summary line.

name: Series-builds-a-shape explainer
summary: A curious, one-idea explainer that builds a complex shape by stacking simple waves.
bestFor: STEM channels and curious-mind explainers
prompt: A 60 second explainer showing how a wave series builds any shape. Start with one smooth wave, add a second and a third, and watch the sum grow closer to a sharp square shape. Keep the tone playful, label each added wave, and end with an invitation to ask about anything you are curious about.

name: Shard logo assembly
summary: A logo draws as wireframe, then faceted shards fly in and lock it together.
bestFor: App launches and brand intros
prompt: Open with a fictional app logo drawn as a thin wireframe outline. Then faceted low-poly shards fly in one by one, each landing with a small settle, until the full logo is assembled. Finish by bringing in the app icon background and typing out the brand name letter by letter. Slow, confident reveal.

name: Stop-motion product story
summary: A hand-drawn stop-motion first-person story where the product explains itself.
bestFor: Fintech apps and personable explainers
prompt: Tell a first-person story where a fictional savings app introduces itself in a hand-drawn stop-motion style, with slightly jittery lines and paper cutouts. It states the problem people have with idle money, shows what it does about it, and signs off with a friendly line. Warm, honest voice and simple drawn props.

name: Capability progression timeline
summary: A rapid month-by-month timeline showing a technology leaping forward and where it heads next.
bestFor: Tech recaps, roadmaps and trend reviews
prompt: Build a fast timeline of one year of progress in a fictional product line. Each month slams in as a big label with a new release and one capability it unlocked, with hard cuts on the beat. Build momentum, then end on a forward-looking trajectory arrow pointing at what comes next. Bang, bang, boom pacing, no dead space.

name: Poster breaks frame
summary: A poster design that cracks its border and spills its elements out of the frame.
bestFor: Event promos, brand teasers and design showreels
prompt: Start on a neatly framed poster for a fictional music night with a bold headline, border and shapes. Then the elements push against the border, the frame cracks, and the headline, shapes and details burst out past the edges and take over the full screen. Finish on a clean full-bleed lockup of the event name and date.

name: Budget app promo
summary: A smooth promo for a fictional household budget app with clean screens and one cursor action per beat.
bestFor: Personal finance apps and consumer app launches
prompt: Make a short promo for a fictional household budget app. Show the problem of scattered receipts, then clean app screens where a cursor adds an expense, categories sort themselves, and the monthly overview fills in. Calm, soft colours, each screen arriving with a gentle slide, and a closing line about knowing where money goes.

name: Fast feature launch
summary: A quick launch video that flashes each key feature in a fast, brand-coloured sequence.
bestFor: SaaS launches and feature announcements
prompt: Create a fast-paced launch video under twenty seconds for a fictional project tool. Open with a one-line hook, then flash four key features in quick succession, each with a big label and a tiny UI action such as a click or toggle. Keep every beat short, use bold brand colour, and end on the product name with a call to action.

name: Oscilloscope studio intro
summary: A glowing line-trace studio intro where waveforms draw the name and services.
bestFor: Design studios and creative agencies
prompt: Introduce a fictional design studio in an oscilloscope style. Glowing thin lines trace across a dark grid, wobbling like waveforms before settling into the studio name. Then each service appears as a line-drawn icon traced by the signal, with soft scanline flicker. End on a steady lockup with the studio name and a contact line.

name: Risograph studio intro
summary: A grainy two-colour risograph studio intro with offset print layers and stamped type.
bestFor: Creative studios and print-minded brands
prompt: Introduce a fictional creative studio in a risograph print style. Two spot colours overprint with slight misregistration, paper grain and halftone dots. Type stamps in with offset layers, shapes slide in like separate print passes, and each service gets a printed label. Close on the studio name and a simple call to get in touch.

name: Cocktail recipe how-to
summary: A step-by-step cocktail build from empty glass to garnish with ingredients and measures labelled.
bestFor: Recipe creators, bars and food brands
prompt: Show a full cocktail recipe from an empty glass to the finished drink in explainer style. Each ingredient pours or drops in with its name and measurement shown beside it, then a stir, ice and a garnish land to complete it. Warm, simple illustrated shapes, a clear order of steps, and a final title card with the drink name.

name: Neon history timeline
summary: A year-by-year company history where neon dates slam in and line drawings add each milestone.
bestFor: Company histories, anniversaries and brand stories
prompt: Tell the short history of a fictional company as a timeline. Each year appears as a large neon number that spins in with a springy 3D turn and lands hard. A simple line drawing then sketches in the milestone for that year, from a small workshop to a larger group. Close on a single line about what comes next. Fast and punchy.

name: Step-by-step recipe
summary: An empty glass fills ingredient by ingredient with measures labelled as each one lands.
bestFor: Recipes, drinks, food brands, cooking channels
prompt: Make a 30 second recipe explainer for a signature iced coffee cocktail. Start on an empty glass, then add each ingredient one at a time with its measure written beside it, the liquid rising and the layers settling. Finish on the complete drink with its name and a short serving tip.

name: Doodle civilisation story
summary: A wordless hand-drawn story of progress, from first spark to a hatching idea, warm and poetic.
bestFor: Brand origin stories, mission films, thought-leadership
prompt: Make a 45 second wordless doodle story of how people built tools, towns and machines until a new idea hatched from an egg. Warm paper background, cute hand-drawn figures, almost no text so any viewer can follow it. End softly on the company name.

name: Concept flow explainer
summary: Nodes and links draw across the screen to show how one idea passes value to another.
bestFor: SEO, marketing and finance concepts that are hard to picture
prompt: Make a 40 second visual explainer of how a trusted site passing credit to a smaller site works, using nodes and drawn links. Begin with one lonely page, add pages that point to it, show the weight of each link growing, then end on the result for the page. Clean diagrams, one idea per beat.

name: Concept overlay cuts
summary: Short full-screen graphic cuts that turn spoken ideas into simple, on-brand visuals.
bestFor: Podcasts, interviews and talking-head videos that need visual relief
prompt: Make a set of short full-screen graphic moments to cut into a talking episode. Each one turns a hard idea into a simple picture, such as a contract clause splitting into plain words. Use one monochrome style with typewriter labels and hand-drawn marks, and keep captions faithful to what is said.

name: Kinetic poster bumper
summary: A loopable square bumper of loud poster type slamming in, hit by hit, in two hot colours.
bestFor: Creator channel intros, social bumpers and brand stings
prompt: Make a 20 second looping square bumper in black with magenta and acid green accents. Six short slogans slam in one after another in huge condensed type, with tiny mono labels as supporting crumbs and a slight print misregister on impact. The last frame matches the first so it loops.

name: One-shape product story
summary: A cursor walks a single morphing card through a product's key screens, from sign-up to match, on the beat.
bestFor: Product tours for apps with a clear user journey
prompt: Make a 30 second tour of a community app where one card morphs between screens without a cut. A cursor taps join, types a handle, confirms a prompt, watches a globe fill with members, switches tabs, replies to an invite and searches, then returns to the logo. Every state is a real screen, on a steady beat.

name: Milestone launch announcement
summary: A fast launch-style video that celebrates a milestone and points viewers to try the product.
bestFor: Startup milestone posts and thank-you announcements
prompt: Make a 20 second announcement video celebrating that a design tool reached a big audience milestone within months of launch. Open on the number counting up, show three quick product moments, thank the community in one line, and close with the product name and a call to try it.

name: Portfolio showreel
summary: A premium resume showreel that frames real site screens in browser and phone frames, cut on the beat.
bestFor: Developers, designers and consultants showing their work
prompt: Make a 60 second showreel for a developer advocate's portfolio. Show home, writing and contact pages inside browser and phone frames, with a chat box answering questions in large bold type. Use three brand colours, one idea per shot, eased motion, and cut each scene on a 120 BPM beat. End on the site and a contact line.

name: Paper theatre story
summary: A vertical paper cut-out shadow theatre scene that answers one human question softly.
bestFor: Brand values films, vertical shorts and emotional storytelling
prompt: Make a 40 second vertical paper cut-out shadow theatre film on the question of what makes a place feel like home. Layered paper silhouettes of a window, a lamp, a kettle and a doorway slide in with soft shadows and warm light, with gentle music and only a few words of text.

name: Feature launch trailer
summary: A polished SaaS launch trailer that pairs each feature with the benefit it brings, scene by scene.
bestFor: SaaS teams announcing a product or major feature release
prompt: Make a 30 second launch trailer for a slide-making app. Each scene shows one feature in a clean UI card, with a bold line naming the benefit, such as building a deck from a sentence. Keep a confident, edited pace with smooth transitions and finish on the product name and a try-it prompt.
